proofs.proof_tex:
The target of every call on the chain is fixed at \(C=D_i\) by \(\mathrm{def:success\text{-}or\text{-}certificate\text{-}algorithm}\). At a terminal failure,
\[
 C\subsetneq T\subseteq T_i^{(0)},\qquad
 \operatorname{SComp}_{G^S}(C)=\{C\},\qquad
 \operatorname{SComp}_{G^S}(T)=\{T\},\qquad
 \operatorname{An}_{G^S[T]}(C)=T.
\]
These are exactly the clauses of \(\operatorname{SHedge}_{G^S}(C,T)\) in \(\mathrm{def:s\text{-}hedge}\).

Apply \(\mathrm{lem:projection\text{-}components}\) with \(H=C\) and \(H=T\). The two singleton S-component identities imply that \(\Pi_S(G^S)[C]\) and \(\Pi_S(G^S)[T]\) each have one district. Projection preserves all and only directed edges with endpoints in \(N_S\), so
\[
 \operatorname{An}_{\Pi_S(G^S)[T]}(C)
 =\operatorname{An}_{G^S[T]}(C)=T.
\]
Choose a bidirected spanning tree \(K_0\) of \(\Pi_S(G^S)[C]\). Starting from \(K_0\), repeatedly attach a vertex outside the current set by the first edge on a bidirected path to that set; this gives a spanning tree \(K_1\) of \(\Pi_S(G^S)[T]\) with \(K_1[C]=K_0\). Put \(R=C\). Give \(F_0\) vertex set \(C\), bidirected tree \(K_0\), and no directed edges. For \(t\in T\setminus C\), define
\[
 d(t)=\min\{\ell:\text{a directed path of length }\ell
 \text{ runs from }t\text{ to }C\text{ in }G^S[T]\}.
\]
The ancestral equality makes \(d(t)\) finite. Choose a next vertex \(c(t)\) on a shortest path and put \(t\to c(t)\) in \(F_1\). Since \(d(c(t))=d(t)-1\), there is no directed cycle; vertices outside \(C\) have one child and vertices in \(C\) have none. With bidirected tree \(K_1\), \(F_1\) is an \(R\)-rooted \(C\)-forest and \(F_1[C]=F_0\).

From \(D=\operatorname{An}_{G^S[N_S\setminus X_N]}(Y_N)\) and \(C=D_i\subseteq D\),
\[
 C\cap X_N=\varnothing,\qquad
 R=C\subseteq\operatorname{An}_{G^S[N_S\setminus X_N]}(Y_N)
 =\operatorname{An}_{\Pi_S(G^S)[N_S\setminus X_N]}(Y_N).
\]
If \(T\cap X_N=\varnothing\), every \(t\in T\) reaches \(C\), and every vertex of \(C\) reaches \(Y_N\), inside \(N_S\setminus X_N\). Thus \(T\subseteq D\). Since \(T\) is one S-component containing the S-component \(D_i=C\) of \(D\), maximality of \(D_i\) gives \(T\subseteq C\), contrary to \(C\subsetneq T\). Hence \(T\cap X_N\ne\varnothing\).

If \(\operatorname{NativeForestTrace}(G^S;X,Y)\) holds, its terminal-trace clause supplies forests with the same vertex, root, and incidence properties whose edges all belong to \(G^S[N_S]\). This proves the native conclusion. No step constructs a causal model.

For \(r\in\{0,1\}\), substitute \(q_C^{(r)}\), the common \(q_j\) for \(D_j\ne C\), and the common \(p^S\) into \(\mathrm{def:eq23\text{-}functional}\). Finiteness permits termwise subtraction, and distributivity gives
\[
 \Phi^{(0)}(y)-\Phi^{(1)}(y)
 =\sum_{w,d_{D\setminus Y_N}}
 p^S(y_S,w\mid x_S)
 \bigl(q_C^{(0)}-q_C^{(1)}\bigr)
 \prod_{D_j\ne C}q_j
 =\Delta(y).
\]
Two measures on finite \(Y\) are unequal exactly when one point mass is unequal, proving the equivalence.

Positivity does not make this contraction injective. For binary \((A,R)\), take
\[
 q_C^{(0)}(0,0)=q_C^{(0)}(1,1)=\frac38,\quad
 q_C^{(0)}(1,0)=q_C^{(0)}(0,1)=\frac18,\quad
 q_C^{(1)}(a,r)=\frac14.
\]
Both kernels are positive and unequal, but for each \(r\),
\[
 \sum_a\bigl(q_C^{(0)}(a,r)-q_C^{(1)}(a,r)\bigr)=0.
\]
If \(A\subseteq D\setminus Y_N\) is marginalized and all common factors are independent of \(A\), the contraction contains this zero sum, so \(\Delta(y)=0\) for every \(y\). This is the claimed obstruction.

The recursion assertions are \(\mathrm{lem:sid\text{-}graph\text{-}recursion\text{-}termination}\). For supplied \(E_0,E_1\), \(\mathrm{def:certificate\text{-}checker}\) exhaustively enumerates finite latent, observational, and outcome cells and has the displayed operation bound. By \(\mathrm{lem:certificate\text{-}checker\text{-}soundness}\), acceptance places both realizations in \(\mathfrak M_+(G^S,\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}})\), proves equality and positivity of their selected laws, and proves target inequality at \(x_{\mathrm{bin}}\). Neither premise constructs a certificate, so no totality conclusion follows.

added_lemmas.statement: Let \(F_0\subset F_1\) be finite nested common-\(R\)-rooted \(C\)-forests in a semi-Markovian ADMG, with \(C\cap X_N=\varnothing\), \(V(F_1)\cap X_N\ne\varnothing\), and \(R\subseteq\operatorname{An}_{G[N_S\setminus X_N]}(Y_N)\). The positive finite-state completeness construction of Kivva et al. supplies an odd integer \(\kappa>4\), finite state spaces, and two semi-Markovian SCMs using the forest incidence that have the same strictly positive observational distribution but, at a common treatment value, have different postintervention distributions on \(R\).

added_lemmas.justification: This is the published positive finite multistate substrate used only on actual-edge ordinary forests.
added_lemmas.gap: The source does not lift virtual edges through selection ancestors or provide binary rational certificates.
added_lemmas.consumer: The native separator specializes this construction to a terminal native forest.

added_lemmas.statement: If \(\operatorname{NativeForestTrace}(G^S;X,Y)\) holds, then \(G^S\) is an admissible finite childless-selector augmented ADMG for the published latent S-ID problem. For every finite signature \(\sigma\), the class \(\mathfrak M_+(G^S,\sigma)\) on this restricted trace is exactly the exact-induced-graph positive compatibility class of \(\mathrm{def:model\text{-}class}\). Hence native-forest traces form a subclass of the published graph instances, without restricting the SCM class on a fixed member graph.
added_lemmas.proof_tex: Clause (i) of \(\mathrm{def:native\text{-}forest\text{-}trace}\) gives finiteness, acyclicity, childlessness of \(S\), and the query's disjointness and nonemptiness. These are the published graph and query premises. The definition's final sentence leaves compatibility unchanged. Unfolding \(\mathrm{def:model\text{-}class}\), every \(M\in\mathfrak M_+(G^S,\sigma)\) has exactly the graph parent interfaces, exactly the graph shared-exogenous incidences, mutually independent exogenous variables, and positive selected cells. Thus the native condition restricts only graph traces and selects a subclass of published instances. No strict-inclusion claim is made.
added_lemmas.justification: This certifies that the new scope is a graph subclass of the published setting, not a substituted SCM class.
added_lemmas.gap: No strict-inclusion claim is needed or made.
added_lemmas.consumer: The restricted completeness theorem invokes published soundness on the unchanged exact-graph model class.

added_lemmas.statement:
Assume \(\operatorname{NativeForestTrace}(G^S;X,Y)\), and let \((C,T)\) be an actual terminal Algorithm 1 failure. There exist an odd integer \(\kappa>4\), a finite multistate signature \(\widetilde\sigma_T\) on \(T\), two finite semi-Markovian SCMs \(\overline M_0,\overline M_1\) whose incidences are contained in \(G^S[T]\), the concrete local intervention \(x_{N,T}^\dagger=0_{X_N\cap T}\), and an assignment \(r^\dagger\in\mathcal X_R\) such that
\[
 P_{\overline M_0}(T=t)=P_{\overline M_1}(T=t)>0
 \quad\text{for every }t\in\mathcal X_T,
\]
and
\[
 \delta:=P_{\overline M_0}(R=r^\dagger\mid\operatorname{do}(X_N\cap T=0))
 -P_{\overline M_1}(R=r^\dagger\mid\operatorname{do}(X_N\cap T=0))\ne0.
\]
The signature is the finite Kivva construction, with forest-coordinate alphabets based on \(\{0,\ldots,\kappa\}\) and finite product alphabets elsewhere. No binary, rational, or effective-encoding conclusion is asserted.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
By \(\mathrm{lem:shedge\text{-}projects\text{-}to\text{-}hedge}\) and the native terminal-trace clause, the failure supplies actual-edge nested common-root forests \(F_0\subset F_1\), with \(C\cap X_N=\varnothing\), \(T\cap X_N\ne\varnothing\), and \(R\subseteq\operatorname{An}_{G^S[N_S\setminus X_N]}(Y_N)\). Apply \(\mathrm{lem:kivva\text{-}positive\text{-}finite\text{-}forest\text{-}countermodels}\) to the semi-Markovian graph made from those actual forest edges.

The cited construction chooses odd \(\kappa>4\) and uses \(\{0,\ldots,\kappa\}\)-based finite product alphabets. Relabel the finitely many treatment states, simultaneously in both models, so that its common separating treatment value is denoted \(0_{X_N\cap T}\). Relabeling is a bijection on each state space and therefore preserves every observational atom, its positivity, and the target inequality. This gives \(\widetilde\sigma_T\), \(\overline M_0,\overline M_1\), and \(x_{N,T}^\dagger=0_{X_N\cap T}\). The two postintervention measures on finite \(\mathcal X_R\) are unequal, so some \(r^\dagger\) has unequal point masses; their difference \(\delta\) is nonzero. Every used edge lies in \(F_1\subseteq G^S[T]\). The source supplies finite multistate models, not binary or rational encodings.
added_lemmas.justification: This supplies the load-bearing positive finite separator without claiming unsupported binary or rational strength.
added_lemmas.gap: Kivva et al.'s construction must be applied only where all forest incidences are actual graph edges.
added_lemmas.consumer: The selected extension routes its named root contrast to the original outcome.

added_lemmas.statement: For every finite-signature recursive augmented SCM \(\widetilde M\) whose declared parent interfaces and shared-exogenous incidences induce a subgraph of \(G^S\), \(\operatorname{Exactify}^{\mathrm{fin}}_{G^S}(\widetilde M)\) induces exactly \(G^S\). It has the same observational law and the same postintervention law under every intervention on observed vertices. In particular, strict selected-cell positivity and every intervention-before-conditioning target with positive selection denominator are preserved.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Order the endogenous vertices topologically. Fix every original and fresh exogenous assignment. At the first vertex, the completed function ignores all new parent and latent coordinates, so its output equals the old output. If equality holds at all earlier vertices, coordinate-constancy gives equality at the next vertex. Induction proves pointwise equality of the full endogenous vector.

The fresh factors are independent and normalized, so summing them multiplies every original atom by
\[
 \prod_{U\ \mathrm{fresh}}\sum_uP(U=u)=1.
\]
The observational laws coincide. Under an intervention, the same equations are replaced by the same constants, and the induction applies to the remaining equations; all postintervention laws coincide. Thus selected atoms, selection denominators, and defined conditional targets are preserved.

Every missing directed edge is now in a declared parent interface and every missing bidirected edge has a fresh shared factor. No unlisted incidence was added. The completed induced graph is exactly \(G^S\), and equality of laws preserves positivity.
added_lemmas.justification: The multistate construction needs the same inert exact-graph completion guarantee previously available only for binary certificates.
added_lemmas.gap: This is a representation lemma and does not create a separating pair.
added_lemmas.consumer: The native selected extension uses it after constructing the common law and outcome contrast.

added_lemmas.statement:
Assume \(\operatorname{NativeForestTrace}(G^S;X,Y)\), and let \((C,T)\) be an actual terminal Algorithm 1 failure. Then there exist a finite multistate signature \(\widetilde\sigma\), an intervention value \(x^\dagger\in\mathcal X_X\), two models \(M_0,M_1\in\mathfrak M_+(G^S,\widetilde\sigma)\), and an event \(A_Y\subseteq\mathcal X_Y\) such that
\[
 P_{M_0,\widetilde\sigma}^S(v)=P_{M_1,\widetilde\sigma}^S(v)>0
 \quad\text{for every }v\in\mathcal X_V,
\]
but
\[
 P_{M_0}(A_Y\mid\operatorname{do}(X=x^\dagger),S=1)
 \ne P_{M_1}(A_Y\mid\operatorname{do}(X=x^\dagger),S=1).
\]
Consequently \(\operatorname{Ident}^{\mathrm{fin}}_S(G^S;X,Y)\) is false. The construction is finite and positive but is not claimed binary, rational, or executable.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Use \(\mathrm{lem:positive\text{-}multistate\text{-}native\text{-}forest\text{-}separator}\) and put
\[
 h(a)=P_{\overline M_0}(R=a\mid\operatorname{do}(X_N\cap T=0))
 -P_{\overline M_1}(R=a\mid\operatorname{do}(X_N\cap T=0)),
\]
with \(\delta=h(r^\dagger)\ne0\). For each \(r\in R\), native incidence supplies a path
\[
 \gamma_r:r=v_{r,0}\to\cdots\to v_{r,\ell_r}=y(r),
 \qquad y(r)\in Y_N,
\]
inside \(G^S[N_S\setminus X_N]\). Paths may share vertices or branches.

Augment each path vertex by one signal coordinate for every path through it. The \(r\)-signal has alphabet \(\mathcal X_r\). At its source and each later path vertex use the same randomized-response channel
\[
 K_{\epsilon,r}(z\mid u)
 =(1-\epsilon)\mathbf 1\{z=u\}+\frac{\epsilon}{|\mathcal X_r|},
 \qquad 0<\epsilon<1.
\]
Use independent finite private noises, and product channels at shared vertices. Retain the Kivva base coordinates on \(T\), and give all other base coordinates independent full-support laws. Conditional on the base vector on \(T\), all new coordinates have one common strictly positive conditional kernel. Equality and positivity of the base laws therefore imply
\[
 P_0(V=v)=P_1(V=v)>0
\]
for every augmented state \(v\).

Give all vertices in \(A_S\) identical independent full-support mechanisms, and make \(S\) an independent fair bit while ignoring its declared parents. Then
\[
 P_j(V=v,S=1)=\frac12P_j(V=v)>0,\qquad
 P_j(V=v\mid S=1)=P_j(V=v),
\]
so the selected laws agree.

Let \(L=\sum_{r\in R}(\ell_r+1)\). Couple every channel as exact copying with probability \(1-\epsilon\) and uniform redrawing with probability \(\epsilon\). All terminal signals equal their root inputs with probability at least \((1-\epsilon)^L\). If \(A_Y\) is the event that the terminal signal tuple equals \(r^\dagger\), then for \(j=0,1\),
\[
 \left|P_j(A_Y\mid\operatorname{do}(X=x^\dagger))
 -P_{\overline M_j}(R=r^\dagger\mid\operatorname{do}(X_N\cap T=0))\right|
 \le1-(1-\epsilon)^L.
\]
Here \(x^\dagger\) uses Kivva's zero levels on \(X_N\cap T\) and fixed values elsewhere. The paths avoid \(X_N\), so intervention cuts no signal channel. Choose \(\epsilon\) with
\[
 2\{1-(1-\epsilon)^L\}<|\delta|.
\]
The triangle inequality yields
\[
 |P_0(A_Y\mid\operatorname{do}(X=x^\dagger))
 -P_1(A_Y\mid\operatorname{do}(X=x^\dagger))|
 \ge|\delta|-2\{1-(1-\epsilon)^L\}>0.
\]
Independence of \(S\) persists after intervention, so conditioning on \(S=1\) changes neither target.

All used forest and routing edges are actual edges of \(G^S\); the premodels induce subgraphs of \(G^S\). Apply \(\operatorname{Exactify}^{\mathrm{fin}}_{G^S}\). By \(\mathrm{lem:finite\text{-}exactification\text{-}preserves\text{-}laws}\), the completed models induce exactly \(G^S\) and preserve the equal positive selected law and target contrast. They lie in \(\mathfrak M_+(G^S,\widetilde\sigma)\). This one finite-signature pair falsifies \(\mathrm{def:graphwise\text{-}sid}\).
added_lemmas.justification: This constructs a full selected-law counterpair and proves noncancellation at the SCM level.
added_lemmas.gap: The common-channel proof relies on actual forest and routing edges and does not cover virtual selection-ancestor paths.
added_lemmas.consumer: It is the necessity step in native-forest graphwise completeness.

added_lemmas.statement: Whenever published Algorithm 1 reaches its single-component recursion, every call chain terminates. A recursive step with fixed target \(C=D_i\) replaces \(T\) by the S-component \(T'\) containing \(D_i\) inside \(A=\operatorname{An}_{G^S[T]}(D_i)\), where \(T'\subseteq A\subsetneq T\). Hence \(\rho\) decreases strictly. The chain rooted at \(T_i^{(0)}\) has at most \(|T_i^{(0)}|\) invocations, its depth is at most \(|N_S|\), and the total number of single-component invocations is at most \(B_0\).
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Fix \((D_i,T_i^{(0)})\). Every call keeps \(C=D_i\). Recursion occurs only when
\[
 C\subsetneq A:=\operatorname{An}_{G^S[T]}(C)\subsetneq T.
\]
The next enclosure is the S-component \(T'\) of \(A\) containing \(C\), whence
\[
 \varnothing\ne C\subseteq T'\subseteq A\subsetneq T,\qquad |T'|\le|T|-1.
\]
Thus each step replaces a positive entry \(|T|\) of \(\rho\) by a strictly smaller one. Equivalently, \(|T|\) decreases strictly on each chain, excluding an infinite chain. If \(|T_i^{(0)}|=m\), there are at most \(m-1\) decreases and at most \(m\) invocations. Since \(T_i^{(0)}\subseteq N_S\), depth is at most \(|N_S|\). Summing and using \(\mathrm{def:initial\text{-}call\text{-}budget}\),
\[
 \#\{\text{single-component invocations}\}
 \le\sum_{(D_i,T_i^{(0)})\in\mathcal I_0}|T_i^{(0)}|=B_0.
\]
Finiteness of \(G^S\) makes all bounds finite.
added_lemmas.justification: Termination is independent of whether failure certificates can be compiled.
added_lemmas.gap: The bound counts graph-recursion calls and not certificate-construction work.
added_lemmas.consumer: Both the native completeness theorem and the non-total executable theorem use this finite dichotomy.

added_lemmas.statement:
Let \(\operatorname{NativeForestTrace}(G^S;X,Y)\) hold. Then published Algorithm 1 succeeds on \((G^S,X,Y)\) if and only if \(\operatorname{Ident}^{\mathrm{fin}}_S(G^S;X,Y)\) holds. On success, for every finite signature \(\sigma\), every \(x\in\prod_{v\in X}\mathcal X_v\), and every \(M\in\mathfrak M_+(G^S,\sigma)\),
\[
 \Phi_{23,x}^{\sigma}(P_{M,\sigma}^S)=\Theta_{x,\sigma}(M),
\]
with the outer conditional evaluated at \(x_S\) and every recursive kernel at \(x_N\). On terminal failure, \(\mathrm{lem:native\text{-}forest\text{-}selected\text{-}extension}\) supplies one finite multistate signature and two exact-graph models with one common strictly positive selected law and unequal intervention-before-conditioning targets. No binary, rational, or executable failure certificate is claimed.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
By \(\mathrm{lem:native\text{-}forest\text{-}trace\text{-}subclass}\), this is within the published exact-graph setting. If Algorithm 1 succeeds, \(\mathrm{lem:published\text{-}latent\text{-}sid\text{-}soundness}\) gives
\[
 \Phi_{23,x}^{\sigma}(P_{M,\sigma}^S)=\Theta_{x,\sigma}(M)
\]
for every \(\sigma,x,M\). Selected-cell positivity defines the observational conditionals, and \(\mathrm{lem:target\text{-}support}\) gives a positive postintervention selection denominator. Equal selected laws therefore give equal functional values and equal targets. By \(\mathrm{def:graphwise\text{-}sid}\), \(\operatorname{Ident}^{\mathrm{fin}}_S(G^S;X,Y)\) holds.

Conversely, the native definition makes the initial check pass. By \(\mathrm{lem:sid\text{-}graph\text{-}recursion\text{-}termination}\), nonsuccess reaches a terminal failure. Then \(\mathrm{lem:native\text{-}forest\text{-}selected\text{-}extension}\) gives a finite \(\widetilde\sigma\), \(x^\dagger\), and \(M_0,M_1\in\mathfrak M_+(G^S,\widetilde\sigma)\) with
\[
 P_{M_0,\widetilde\sigma}^S=P_{M_1,\widetilde\sigma}^S>0,\qquad
 \Theta_{x^\dagger,\widetilde\sigma}(M_0)\ne
 \Theta_{x^\dagger,\widetilde\sigma}(M_1).
\]
This single within-signature pair falsifies the universal implication in \(\mathrm{def:graphwise\text{-}sid}\). Thus failure implies nonidentification, completing the equivalence.
added_lemmas.justification: This is the proved graphwise converse on the maximal scope supported by the actual-incidence construction.
added_lemmas.gap: Universal completeness remains open for virtual edges and initial-check failures.
added_lemmas.consumer: Graphical analysts obtain an exact success criterion and a finite positive countermodel witness on native traces.

added_lemmas.statement: Does there exist \(x_\star\in\{0,1\}^{X_\star}\) and \(E_{\star,0},E_{\star,1}\in\operatorname{CertSCM}(G_\star^S,\sigma_{\mathrm{bin},\star})\) such that the exact checker accepts, their realized models have the same strictly positive selected law on every cell of \(\{0,1\}^{V_\star}\), and \(Q_{\star,x_\star}(\llbracket E_{\star,0}\rrbracket)\ne Q_{\star,x_\star}(\llbracket E_{\star,1}\rrbracket)\)? The known support-deficient pair has targets \(1/2\) and \(5/8\), but does not answer this positive-binary question.
added_lemmas.justification: This preserves the binary strengthening as a precise open stress test.
added_lemmas.gap: The known separating pair is support deficient, and two natural positivity repairs provably erase its contrast.
added_lemmas.consumer: A positive exact answer would be the first base case for the universal rational inverse lift.

added_lemmas.statement: For every finite childless-selector augmented ADMG \(G^S\), including graphs whose terminal S-Hedges require virtual bidirected edges through shared or branching selection ancestors and instances failing the initial d-separation check, does published Algorithm 1 succeed if and only if \(\operatorname{Ident}^{\mathrm{fin}}_S(G^S;X,Y)\) holds? Equivalently, can every failure be converted into a finite-signature exact-graph pair with one common strictly positive selected law and unequal intervention-before-conditioning targets? The native-forest theorem answers this only on \(\operatorname{NativeForestTrace}(G^S;X,Y)\).
added_lemmas.justification: This preserves Abouei et al.'s unrestricted completeness conjecture without presenting it as proved.
added_lemmas.gap: Virtual-edge inverse realization and the initial-failure compiler are both missing.
added_lemmas.consumer: It records the exact frontier beyond the native-incidence theorem.

added_lemmas.statement: Whenever the initial selected d-separation check of published Algorithm 1 fails, can one effectively choose \(x_{\mathrm{bin}}\) and construct \(E_0,E_1\in\operatorname{CertSCM}(G^S,\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}})\) with rational finite tables such that \(\mathsf{Check}_{\mathrm{NONID}}(G^S,X,Y,x_{\mathrm{bin}},E_0,E_1)=\mathrm{accept}\)? The definition of \(\mathsf{AncestorPair}\) names this desired output but does not prove that the compiler exists.
added_lemmas.justification: This keeps the initial-failure compiler separate from terminal S-Hedge lifting.
added_lemmas.gap: The intended construction is named but no finite rational accepted certificate is derived.
added_lemmas.consumer: Universal completeness and total compilation both require it.

added_lemmas.statement: Can \(\mathsf{sID}^{\pm}\) be made total by two effective finite-rational compilers: one for failure of the initial selected d-separation check and one for every terminal recursive S-Hedge, each returning an accepted exact-graph \(\operatorname{CertSCM}\) pair? A positive answer requires both the independent \(\mathsf{AncestorPair}\) compiler and the compositional inverse lift with noncancelling outcome contrast; graph-recursion termination and checker verification alone do not construct either pair.
added_lemmas.justification: This separates total compilation from the proved recursion and checker bounds.
added_lemmas.gap: Both independent exact-rational failure compilers are absent.
added_lemmas.consumer: Future software totality requires a positive answer.

proposed_statement_changes.current: For every finite signature \(\sigma\), fix \(D_i\in\mathcal D_S(D)\), let \(T_i^{(0)}\) be the unique member of \(\operatorname{SComp}_{G^S}(N_S)\) containing \(D_i\), and consider the call chain of \(\operatorname{sID\text{-}Single}(D_i,T_i^{(0)},Q_{P_\sigma}^S[T_i^{(0)}])\). If this chain fails at \((C,T)\), then \(C=D_i\), \(C\subsetneq T\subseteq T_i^{(0)}\), \(\operatorname{SComp}_{G^S}(C)=\{C\}\), \(\operatorname{SComp}_{G^S}(T)=\{T\}\), and \(\operatorname{An}_{G^S[T]}(C)=T\), so \(\operatorname{SHedge}_{G^S}(C,T)\). Moreover, \(\Pi_S(G^S)[C]\) and \(\Pi_S(G^S)[T]\) are single districts, \(\operatorname{An}_{\Pi_S(G^S)[T]}(C)=T\), and one can construct \(R=C\) and nested common-\(R\)-rooted \(C\)-forests \(F_0\subset F_1\) with vertex sets \(C\) and \(T\) satisfying \(C\cap X_N=\varnothing\), \(T\cap X_N\ne\varnothing\), and \(R\subseteq\operatorname{An}_{\Pi_S(G^S)[N_S\setminus X_N]}(Y_N)\). This graph-theoretic conclusion does not assert the existence of a strictly positive rational projected countermodel pair.
proposed_statement_changes.proposed: For every finite signature \(\sigma\), fix \(D_i\in\mathcal D_S(D)\), let \(T_i^{(0)}\) be the unique member of \(\operatorname{SComp}_{G^S}(N_S)\) containing \(D_i\), and consider the call chain of \(\operatorname{sID\text{-}Single}(D_i,T_i^{(0)},Q_{P_\sigma}^S[T_i^{(0)}])\). If this chain fails at \((C,T)\), then \(C=D_i\), \(C\subsetneq T\subseteq T_i^{(0)}\), \(\operatorname{SComp}_{G^S}(C)=\{C\}\), \(\operatorname{SComp}_{G^S}(T)=\{T\}\), and \(\operatorname{An}_{G^S[T]}(C)=T\), so \(\operatorname{SHedge}_{G^S}(C,T)\). Moreover, \(\Pi_S(G^S)[C]\) and \(\Pi_S(G^S)[T]\) are single districts, \(\operatorname{An}_{\Pi_S(G^S)[T]}(C)=T\), and there are nested common-\(R\)-rooted \(C\)-forests \(F_0\subset F_1\) in the projection, with \(R=C\), vertex sets \(C\) and \(T\), and \(C\cap X_N=\varnothing\), \(T\cap X_N\ne\varnothing\), and \(R\subseteq\operatorname{An}_{\Pi_S(G^S)[N_S\setminus X_N]}(Y_N)\). If \(\operatorname{NativeForestTrace}(G^S;X,Y)\) also holds, the forests can instead be chosen as subgraphs of \(G^S[N_S]\), so every directed and bidirected forest edge is an actual edge of the original nonancestor graph and \(R\subseteq\operatorname{An}_{G^S[N_S\setminus X_N]}(Y_N)\). The target of every call on the chain is fixed at \(C=D_i\) by \(\mathrm{def:success\text{-}or\text{-}certificate\text{-}algorithm}\). At a terminal failure,
\[
 C\subsetneq T\subseteq T_i^{(0)},\qquad

 \operatorname{SComp}_{G^S}(T)=\{T\},\qquad
 \operatorname{An}_{G^S[T]}(C)=T.
\]
These are exactly the clauses of \(\operatorname{SHedge}_{G^S}(C,T)\) in \(\mathrm{def:s\text{-}hedge}\).

Apply \(\mathrm{lem:projection\text{-}components}\) with \(H=C\) and \(H=T\). The two singleton S-component identities imply that \(\Pi_S(G^S)[C]\) and \(\Pi_S(G^S)[T]\) each have one district. Projection preserves all and only directed edges with endpoints in \(N_S\), so
\[
 \operatorname{An}_{\Pi_S(G^S)[T]}(C)
 =\operatorname{An}_{G^S[T]}(C)=T.
\]
Choose a bidirected spanning tree \(K_0\) of \(\Pi_S(G^S)[C]\). Starting from \(K_0\), repeatedly attach a vertex outside the current set by the first edge on a bidirected path to that set; this gives a spanning tree \(K_1\) of \(\Pi_S(G^S)[T]\) with \(K_1[C]=K_0\). Put \(R=C\). Give \(F_0\) vertex set \(C\), bidirected tree \(K_0\), and no directed edges. For \(t\in T\setminus C\), define
\[
 d(t)=\min\{\ell:\text{a directed path of length }\ell
 \text{ runs from }t\text{ to }C\text{ in }G^S[T]\}.
\]
The ancestral equality makes \(d(t)\) finite. Choose a next vertex \(c(t)\) on a shortest path and put \(t\to c(t)\) in \(F_1\). Since \(d(c(t))=d(t)-1\), there is no directed cycle; vertices outside \(C\) have one child and vertices in \(C\) have none. With bidirected tree \(K_1\), \(F_1\) is an \(R\)-rooted \(C\)-forest and \(F_1[C]=F_0\).

From \(D=\operatorname{An}_{G^S[N_S\setminus X_N]}(Y_N)\) and \(C=D_i\subseteq D\),
\[
 C\cap X_N=\varnothing,\qquad
 R=C\subseteq\operatorname{An}_{G^S[N_S\setminus X_N]}(Y_N)
 =\operatorname{An}_{\Pi_S(G^S)[N_S\setminus X_N]}(Y_N).
\]
If \(T\cap X_N=\varnothing\), every \(t\in T\) reaches \(C\), and every vertex of \(C\) reaches \(Y_N\), inside \(N_S\setminus X_N\). Thus \(T\subseteq D\). Since \(T\) is one S-component containing the S-component \(D_i=C\) of \(D\), maximality of \(D_i\) gives \(T\subseteq C\), contrary to \(C\subsetneq T\). Hence \(T\cap X_N\ne\varnothing\).

If \(\operatorname{NativeForestTrace}(G^S;X,Y)\) holds, its terminal-trace clause supplies forests with the same vertex, root, and incidence properties whose edges all belong to \(G^S[N_S]\). This proves the native conclusion. No step constructs a causal model.

For \(r\in\{0,1\}\), substitute \(q_C^{(r)}\), the common \(q_j\) for \(D_j\ne C\), and the common \(p^S\) into \(\mathrm{def:eq23\text{-}functional}\). Finiteness permits termwise subtraction, and distributivity gives
\[
 \Phi^{(0)}(y)-\Phi^{(1)}(y)
 =\sum_{w,d_{D\setminus Y_N}}
 p^S(y_S,w\mid x_S)
 \bigl(q_C^{(0)}-q_C^{(1)}\bigr)
 \prod_{D_j\ne C}q_j
 =\Delta(y).
\]
Two measures on finite \(Y\) are unequal exactly when one point mass is unequal, proving the equivalence.

Positivity does not make this contraction injective. For binary \((A,R)\), take
\[
 q_C^{(0)}(0,0)=q_C^{(0)}(1,1)=\frac38,\quad
 q_C^{(0)}(1,0)=q_C^{(0)}(0,1)=\frac18,\quad
 q_C^{(1)}(a,r)=\frac14.
\]
Both kernels are positive and unequal, but for each \(r\),
\[
 \sum_a\bigl(q_C^{(0)}(a,r)-q_C^{(1)}(a,r)\bigr)=0.
\]
If \(A\subseteq D\setminus Y_N\) is marginalized and all common factors are independent of \(A\), the contraction contains this zero sum, so \(\Delta(y)=0\) for every \(y\). This is the claimed obstruction.

The recursion assertions are \(\mathrm{lem:sid\text{-}graph\text{-}recursion\text{-}termination}\). For supplied \(E_0,E_1\), \(\mathrm{def:certificate\text{-}checker}\) exhaustively enumerates finite latent, observational, and outcome cells and has the displayed operation bound. By \(\mathrm{lem:certificate\text{-}checker\text{-}soundness}\), acceptance places both realizations in \(\mathfrak M_+(G^S,\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}})\), proves equality and positivity of their selected laws, and proves target inequality at \(x_{\mathrm{bin}}\). Neither premise constructs a certificate, so no totality conclusion follows.

added_lemmas.statement: Let \(F_0\subset F_1\) be finite nested common-\(R\)-rooted \(C\)-forests in a semi-Markovian ADMG, with \(C\cap X_N=\varnothing\), \(V(F_1)\cap X_N\ne\varnothing\), and \(R\subseteq\operatorname{An}_{G[N_S\setminus X_N]}(Y_N)\). The positive finite-state completeness construction of Kivva et al. supplies an odd integer \(\kappa>4\), finite state spaces, and two semi-Markovian SCMs using the forest incidence that have the same strictly positive observational distribution but, at a common treatment value, have different postintervention distributions on \(R\).

added_lemmas.justification: This is the published positive finite multistate substrate used only on actual-edge ordinary forests.
added_lemmas.gap: The source does not lift virtual edges through selection ancestors or provide binary rational certificates.
added_lemmas.consumer: The native separator specializes this construction to a terminal native forest.

added_lemmas.statement: If \(\operatorname{NativeForestTrace}(G^S;X,Y)\) holds, then \(G^S\) is an admissible finite childless-selector augmented ADMG for the published latent S-ID problem. For every finite signature \(\sigma\), the class \(\mathfrak M_+(G^S,\sigma)\) on this restricted trace is exactly the exact-induced-graph positive compatibility class of \(\mathrm{def:model\text{-}class}\). Hence native-forest traces form a subclass of the published graph instances, without restricting the SCM class on a fixed member graph.
added_lemmas.proof_tex: Clause (i) of \(\mathrm{def:native\text{-}forest\text{-}trace}\) gives finiteness, acyclicity, childlessness of \(S\), and the query's disjointness and nonemptiness. These are the published graph and query premises. The definition's final sentence leaves compatibility unchanged. Unfolding \(\mathrm{def:model\text{-}class}\), every \(M\in\mathfrak M_+(G^S,\sigma)\) has exactly the graph parent interfaces, exactly the graph shared-exogenous incidences, mutually independent exogenous variables, and positive selected cells. Thus the native condition restricts only graph traces and selects a subclass of published instances. No strict-inclusion claim is made.
added_lemmas.justification: This certifies that the new scope is a graph subclass of the published setting, not a substituted SCM class.
added_lemmas.gap: No strict-inclusion claim is needed or made.
added_lemmas.consumer: The restricted completeness theorem invokes published soundness on the unchanged exact-graph model class.

added_lemmas.statement:
Assume \(\operatorname{NativeForestTrace}(G^S;X,Y)\), and let \((C,T)\) be an actual terminal Algorithm 1 failure. There exist an odd integer \(\kappa>4\), a finite multistate signature \(\widetilde\sigma_T\) on \(T\), two finite semi-Markovian SCMs \(\overline M_0,\overline M_1\) whose incidences are contained in \(G^S[T]\), the concrete local intervention \(x_{N,T}^\dagger=0_{X_N\cap T}\), and an assignment \(r^\dagger\in\mathcal X_R\) such that
\[
 P_{\overline M_0}(T=t)=P_{\overline M_1}(T=t)>0
 \quad\text{for every }t\in\mathcal X_T,
\]
and
\[
 \delta:=P_{\overline M_0}(R=r^\dagger\mid\operatorname{do}(X_N\cap T=0))
 -P_{\overline M_1}(R=r^\dagger\mid\operatorname{do}(X_N\cap T=0))\ne0.
\]
The signature is the finite Kivva construction, with forest-coordinate alphabets based on \(\{0,\ldots,\kappa\}\) and finite product alphabets elsewhere. No binary, rational, or effective-encoding conclusion is asserted.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
By \(\mathrm{lem:shedge\text{-}projects\text{-}to\text{-}hedge}\) and the native terminal-trace clause, the failure supplies actual-edge nested common-root forests \(F_0\subset F_1\), with \(C\cap X_N=\varnothing\), \(T\cap X_N\ne\varnothing\), and \(R\subseteq\operatorname{An}_{G^S[N_S\setminus X_N]}(Y_N)\). Apply \(\mathrm{lem:kivva\text{-}positive\text{-}finite\text{-}forest\text{-}countermodels}\) to the semi-Markovian graph made from those actual forest edges.

The cited construction chooses odd \(\kappa>4\) and uses \(\{0,\ldots,\kappa\}\)-based finite product alphabets. Relabel the finitely many treatment states, simultaneously in both models, so that its common separating treatment value is denoted \(0_{X_N\cap T}\). Relabeling is a bijection on each state space and therefore preserves every observational atom, its positivity, and the target inequality. This gives \(\widetilde\sigma_T\), \(\overline M_0,\overline M_1\), and \(x_{N,T}^\dagger=0_{X_N\cap T}\). The two postintervention measures on finite \(\mathcal X_R\) are unequal, so some \(r^\dagger\) has unequal point masses; their difference \(\delta\) is nonzero. Every used edge lies in \(F_1\subseteq G^S[T]\). The source supplies finite multistate models, not binary or rational encodings.
added_lemmas.justification: This supplies the load-bearing positive finite separator without claiming unsupported binary or rational strength.
added_lemmas.gap: Kivva et al.'s construction must be applied only where all forest incidences are actual graph edges.
added_lemmas.consumer: The selected extension routes its named root contrast to the original outcome.

added_lemmas.statement: For every finite-signature recursive augmented SCM \(\widetilde M\) whose declared parent interfaces and shared-exogenous incidences induce a subgraph of \(G^S\), \(\operatorname{Exactify}^{\mathrm{fin}}_{G^S}(\widetilde M)\) induces exactly \(G^S\). It has the same observational law and the same postintervention law under every intervention on observed vertices. In particular, strict selected-cell positivity and every intervention-before-conditioning target with positive selection denominator are preserved.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Order the endogenous vertices topologically. Fix every original and fresh exogenous assignment. At the first vertex, the completed function ignores all new parent and latent coordinates, so its output equals the old output. If equality holds at all earlier vertices, coordinate-constancy gives equality at the next vertex. Induction proves pointwise equality of the full endogenous vector.

The fresh factors are independent and normalized, so summing them multiplies every original atom by
\[
 \prod_{U\ \mathrm{fresh}}\sum_uP(U=u)=1.
\]
The observational laws coincide. Under an intervention, the same equations are replaced by the same constants, and the induction applies to the remaining equations; all postintervention laws coincide. Thus selected atoms, selection denominators, and defined conditional targets are preserved.

Every missing directed edge is now in a declared parent interface and every missing bidirected edge has a fresh shared factor. No unlisted incidence was added. The completed induced graph is exactly \(G^S\), and equality of laws preserves positivity.
added_lemmas.justification: The multistate construction needs the same inert exact-graph completion guarantee previously available only for binary certificates.
added_lemmas.gap: This is a representation lemma and does not create a separating pair.
added_lemmas.consumer: The native selected extension uses it after constructing the common law and outcome contrast.

added_lemmas.statement:
Assume \(\operatorname{NativeForestTrace}(G^S;X,Y)\), and let \((C,T)\) be an actual terminal Algorithm 1 failure. Then there exist a finite multistate signature \(\widetilde\sigma\), an intervention value \(x^\dagger\in\mathcal X_X\), two models \(M_0,M_1\in\mathfrak M_+(G^S,\widetilde\sigma)\), and an event \(A_Y\subseteq\mathcal X_Y\) such that
\[
 P_{M_0,\widetilde\sigma}^S(v)=P_{M_1,\widetilde\sigma}^S(v)>0
 \quad\text{for every }v\in\mathcal X_V,
\]
but
\[
 P_{M_0}(A_Y\mid\operatorname{do}(X=x^\dagger),S=1)
 \ne P_{M_1}(A_Y\mid\operatorname{do}(X=x^\dagger),S=1).
\]
Consequently \(\operatorname{Ident}^{\mathrm{fin}}_S(G^S;X,Y)\) is false. The construction is finite and positive but is not claimed binary, rational, or executable.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Use \(\mathrm{lem:positive\text{-}multistate\text{-}native\text{-}forest\text{-}separator}\) and put
\[
 h(a)=P_{\overline M_0}(R=a\mid\operatorname{do}(X_N\cap T=0))
 -P_{\overline M_1}(R=a\mid\operatorname{do}(X_N\cap T=0)),
\]
with \(\delta=h(r^\dagger)\ne0\). For each \(r\in R\), native incidence supplies a path
\[
 \gamma_r:r=v_{r,0}\to\cdots\to v_{r,\ell_r}=y(r),
 \qquad y(r)\in Y_N,
\]
inside \(G^S[N_S\setminus X_N]\). Paths may share vertices or branches.

Augment each path vertex by one signal coordinate for every path through it. The \(r\)-signal has alphabet \(\mathcal X_r\). At its source and each later path vertex use the same randomized-response channel
\[
 K_{\epsilon,r}(z\mid u)
 =(1-\epsilon)\mathbf 1\{z=u\}+\frac{\epsilon}{|\mathcal X_r|},
 \qquad 0<\epsilon<1.
\]
Use independent finite private noises, and product channels at shared vertices. Retain the Kivva base coordinates on \(T\), and give all other base coordinates independent full-support laws. Conditional on the base vector on \(T\), all new coordinates have one common strictly positive conditional kernel. Equality and positivity of the base laws therefore imply
\[
 P_0(V=v)=P_1(V=v)>0
\]
for every augmented state \(v\).

Give all vertices in \(A_S\) identical independent full-support mechanisms, and make \(S\) an independent fair bit while ignoring its declared parents. Then
\[
 P_j(V=v,S=1)=\frac12P_j(V=v)>0,\qquad
 P_j(V=v\mid S=1)=P_j(V=v),
\]
so the selected laws agree.

Let \(L=\sum_{r\in R}(\ell_r+1)\). Couple every channel as exact copying with probability \(1-\epsilon\) and uniform redrawing with probability \(\epsilon\). All terminal signals equal their root inputs with probability at least \((1-\epsilon)^L\). If \(A_Y\) is the event that the terminal signal tuple equals \(r^\dagger\), then for \(j=0,1\),
\[
 \left|P_j(A_Y\mid\operatorname{do}(X=x^\dagger))
 -P_{\overline M_j}(R=r^\dagger\mid\operatorname{do}(X_N\cap T=0))\right|
 \le1-(1-\epsilon)^L.
\]
Here \(x^\dagger\) uses Kivva's zero levels on \(X_N\cap T\) and fixed values elsewhere. The paths avoid \(X_N\), so intervention cuts no signal channel. Choose \(\epsilon\) with
\[
 2\{1-(1-\epsilon)^L\}<|\delta|.
\]
The triangle inequality yields
\[
 |P_0(A_Y\mid\operatorname{do}(X=x^\dagger))
 -P_1(A_Y\mid\operatorname{do}(X=x^\dagger))|
 \ge|\delta|-2\{1-(1-\epsilon)^L\}>0.
\]
Independence of \(S\) persists after intervention, so conditioning on \(S=1\) changes neither target.

All used forest and routing edges are actual edges of \(G^S\); the premodels induce subgraphs of \(G^S\). Apply \(\operatorname{Exactify}^{\mathrm{fin}}_{G^S}\). By \(\mathrm{lem:finite\text{-}exactification\text{-}preserves\text{-}laws}\), the completed models induce exactly \(G^S\) and preserve the equal positive selected law and target contrast. They lie in \(\mathfrak M_+(G^S,\widetilde\sigma)\). This one finite-signature pair falsifies \(\mathrm{def:graphwise\text{-}sid}\).
added_lemmas.justification: This constructs a full selected-law counterpair and proves noncancellation at the SCM level.
added_lemmas.gap: The common-channel proof relies on actual forest and routing edges and does not cover virtual selection-ancestor paths.
added_lemmas.consumer: It is the necessity step in native-forest graphwise completeness.

added_lemmas.statement: Whenever published Algorithm 1 reaches its single-component recursion, every call chain terminates. A recursive step with fixed target \(C=D_i\) replaces \(T\) by the S-component \(T'\) containing \(D_i\) inside \(A=\operatorname{An}_{G^S[T]}(D_i)\), where \(T'\subseteq A\subsetneq T\). Hence \(\rho\) decreases strictly. The chain rooted at \(T_i^{(0)}\) has at most \(|T_i^{(0)}|\) invocations, its depth is at most \(|N_S|\), and the total number of single-component invocations is at most \(B_0\).
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Fix \((D_i,T_i^{(0)})\). Every call keeps \(C=D_i\). Recursion occurs only when
\[
 C\subsetneq A:=\operatorname{An}_{G^S[T]}(C)\subsetneq T.
\]
The next enclosure is the S-component \(T'\) of \(A\) containing \(C\), whence
\[
 \varnothing\ne C\subseteq T'\subseteq A\subsetneq T,\qquad |T'|\le|T|-1.
\]
Thus each step replaces a positive entry \(|T|\) of \(\rho\) by a strictly smaller one. Equivalently, \(|T|\) decreases strictly on each chain, excluding an infinite chain. If \(|T_i^{(0)}|=m\), there are at most \(m-1\) decreases and at most \(m\) invocations. Since \(T_i^{(0)}\subseteq N_S\), depth is at most \(|N_S|\). Summing and using \(\mathrm{def:initial\text{-}call\text{-}budget}\),
\[
 \#\{\text{single-component invocations}\}
 \le\sum_{(D_i,T_i^{(0)})\in\mathcal I_0}|T_i^{(0)}|=B_0.
\]
Finiteness of \(G^S\) makes all bounds finite.
added_lemmas.justification: Termination is independent of whether failure certificates can be compiled.
added_lemmas.gap: The bound counts graph-recursion calls and not certificate-construction work.
added_lemmas.consumer: Both the native completeness theorem and the non-total executable theorem use this finite dichotomy.

added_lemmas.statement:
Let \(\operatorname{NativeForestTrace}(G^S;X,Y)\) hold. Then published Algorithm 1 succeeds on \((G^S,X,Y)\) if and only if \(\operatorname{Ident}^{\mathrm{fin}}_S(G^S;X,Y)\) holds. On success, for every finite signature \(\sigma\), every \(x\in\prod_{v\in X}\mathcal X_v\), and every \(M\in\mathfrak M_+(G^S,\sigma)\),
\[
 \Phi_{23,x}^{\sigma}(P_{M,\sigma}^S)=\Theta_{x,\sigma}(M),
\]
with the outer conditional evaluated at \(x_S\) and every recursive kernel at \(x_N\). On terminal failure, \(\mathrm{lem:native\text{-}forest\text{-}selected\text{-}extension}\) supplies one finite multistate signature and two exact-graph models with one common strictly positive selected law and unequal intervention-before-conditioning targets. No binary, rational, or executable failure certificate is claimed.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
By \(\mathrm{lem:native\text{-}forest\text{-}trace\text{-}subclass}\), this is within the published exact-graph setting. If Algorithm 1 succeeds, \(\mathrm{lem:published\text{-}latent\text{-}sid\text{-}soundness}\) gives
\[
 \Phi_{23,x}^{\sigma}(P_{M,\sigma}^S)=\Theta_{x,\sigma}(M)
\]
for every \(\sigma,x,M\). Selected-cell positivity defines the observational conditionals, and \(\mathrm{lem:target\text{-}support}\) gives a positive postintervention selection denominator. Equal selected laws therefore give equal functional values and equal targets. By \(\mathrm{def:graphwise\text{-}sid}\), \(\operatorname{Ident}^{\mathrm{fin}}_S(G^S;X,Y)\) holds.

Conversely, the native definition makes the initial check pass. By \(\mathrm{lem:sid\text{-}graph\text{-}recursion\text{-}termination}\), nonsuccess reaches a terminal failure. Then \(\mathrm{lem:native\text{-}forest\text{-}selected\text{-}extension}\) gives a finite \(\widetilde\sigma\), \(x^\dagger\), and \(M_0,M_1\in\mathfrak M_+(G^S,\widetilde\sigma)\) with
\[
 P_{M_0,\widetilde\sigma}^S=P_{M_1,\widetilde\sigma}^S>0,\qquad
 \Theta_{x^\dagger,\widetilde\sigma}(M_0)\ne
 \Theta_{x^\dagger,\widetilde\sigma}(M_1).
\]
This single within-signature pair falsifies the universal implication in \(\mathrm{def:graphwise\text{-}sid}\). Thus failure implies nonidentification, completing the equivalence.
added_lemmas.justification: This is the proved graphwise converse on the maximal scope supported by the actual-incidence construction.
added_lemmas.gap: Universal completeness remains open for virtual edges and initial-check failures.
added_lemmas.consumer: Graphical analysts obtain an exact success criterion and a finite positive countermodel witness on native traces.

added_lemmas.statement: Does there exist \(x_\star\in\{0,1\}^{X_\star}\) and \(E_{\star,0},E_{\star,1}\in\operatorname{CertSCM}(G_\star^S,\sigma_{\mathrm{bin},\star})\) such that the exact checker accepts, their realized models have the same strictly positive selected law on every cell of \(\{0,1\}^{V_\star}\), and \(Q_{\star,x_\star}(\llbracket E_{\star,0}\rrbracket)\ne Q_{\star,x_\star}(\llbracket E_{\star,1}\rrbracket)\)? The known support-deficient pair has targets \(1/2\) and \(5/8\), but does not answer this positive-binary question.
added_lemmas.justification: This preserves the binary strengthening as a precise open stress test.
added_lemmas.gap: The known separating pair is support deficient, and two natural positivity repairs provably erase its contrast.
added_lemmas.consumer: A positive exact answer would be the first base case for the universal rational inverse lift.

added_lemmas.statement: For every finite childless-selector augmented ADMG \(G^S\), including graphs whose terminal S-Hedges require virtual bidirected edges through shared or branching selection ancestors and instances failing the initial d-separation check, does published Algorithm 1 succeed if and only if \(\operatorname{Ident}^{\mathrm{fin}}_S(G^S;X,Y)\) holds? Equivalently, can every failure be converted into a finite-signature exact-graph pair with one common strictly positive selected law and unequal intervention-before-conditioning targets? The native-forest theorem answers this only on \(\operatorname{NativeForestTrace}(G^S;X,Y)\).
added_lemmas.justification: This preserves Abouei et al.'s unrestricted completeness conjecture without presenting it as proved.
added_lemmas.gap: Virtual-edge inverse realization and the initial-failure compiler are both missing.
added_lemmas.consumer: It records the exact frontier beyond the native-incidence theorem.

added_lemmas.statement: Whenever the initial selected d-separation check of published Algorithm 1 fails, can one effectively choose \(x_{\mathrm{bin}}\) and construct \(E_0,E_1\in\operatorname{CertSCM}(G^S,\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}})\) with rational finite tables such that \(\mathsf{Check}_{\mathrm{NONID}}(G^S,X,Y,x_{\mathrm{bin}},E_0,E_1)=\mathrm{accept}\)? The definition of \(\mathsf{AncestorPair}\) names this desired output but does not prove that the compiler exists.
added_lemmas.justification: This keeps the initial-failure compiler separate from terminal S-Hedge lifting.
added_lemmas.gap: The intended construction is named but no finite rational accepted certificate is derived.
added_lemmas.consumer: Universal completeness and total compilation both require it.

added_lemmas.statement: Can \(\mathsf{sID}^{\pm}\) be made total by two effective finite-rational compilers: one for failure of the initial selected d-separation check and one for every terminal recursive S-Hedge, each returning an accepted exact-graph \(\operatorname{CertSCM}\) pair? A positive answer requires both the independent \(\mathsf{AncestorPair}\) compiler and the compositional inverse lift with noncancelling outcome contrast; graph-recursion termination and checker verification alone do not construct either pair.
added_lemmas.justification: This separates total compilation from the proved recursion and checker bounds.
added_lemmas.gap: Both independent exact-rational failure compilers are absent.
added_lemmas.consumer: Future software totality requires a positive answer.

proposed_statement_changes.current: For every finite signature \(\sigma\), fix \(D_i\in\mathcal D_S(D)\), let \(T_i^{(0)}\) be the unique member of \(\operatorname{SComp}_{G^S}(N_S)\) containing \(D_i\), and consider the call chain of \(\operatorname{sID\text{-}Single}(D_i,T_i^{(0)},Q_{P_\sigma}^S[T_i^{(0)}])\). If this chain fails at \((C,T)\), then \(C=D_i\), \(C\subsetneq T\subseteq T_i^{(0)}\), \(\operatorname{SComp}_{G^S}(C)=\{C\}\), \(\operatorname{SComp}_{G^S}(T)=\{T\}\), and \(\operatorname{An}_{G^S[T]}(C)=T\), so \(\operatorname{SHedge}_{G^S}(C,T)\). Moreover, \(\Pi_S(G^S)[C]\) and \(\Pi_S(G^S)[T]\) are single districts, \(\operatorname{An}_{\Pi_S(G^S)[T]}(C)=T\), and one can construct \(R=C\) and nested common-\(R\)-rooted \(C\)-forests \(F_0\subset F_1\) with vertex sets \(C\) and \(T\) satisfying \(C\cap X_N=\varnothing\), \(T\cap X_N\ne\varnothing\), and \(R\subseteq\operatorname{An}_{\Pi_S(G^S)[N_S\setminus X_N]}(Y_N)\). This graph-theoretic conclusion does not assert the existence of a strictly positive rational projected countermodel pair.
proposed_statement_changes.proposed: For every finite signature \(\sigma\), fix \(D_i\in\mathcal D_S(D)\), let \(T_i^{(0)}\) be the unique member of \(\operatorname{SComp}_{G^S}(N_S)\) containing \(D_i\), and consider the call chain of \(\operatorname{sID\text{-}Single}(D_i,T_i^{(0)},Q_{P_\sigma}^S[T_i^{(0)}])\). If this chain fails at \((C,T)\), then \(C=D_i\), \(C\subsetneq T\subseteq T_i^{(0)}\), \(\operatorname{SComp}_{G^S}(C)=\{C\}\), \(\operatorname{SComp}_{G^S}(T)=\{T\}\), and \(\operatorname{An}_{G^S[T]}(C)=T\), so \(\operatorname{SHedge}_{G^S}(C,T)\). If \(\operatorname{NativeForestTrace}(G^S;X,Y)\) also holds, the forests can instead be chosen as subgraphs of \(G^S[N_S]\), so every directed and bidirected forest edge is an actual edge of the original nonancestor graph and \(R\subseteq\operatorname{An}_{G^S[N_S\setminus X_N]}(Y_N)\). These are graph-theoretic conclusions only; they assert no binary, rational, or positive countermodel construction.

proofs.proof_tex:
The target of every call on the chain is fixed at \(C=D_i\) by \(\mathrm{def:success\text{-}or\text{-}certificate\text{-}algorithm}\). At a terminal failure,
\[
 C\subsetneq T\subseteq T_i^{(0)},\qquad
 \operatorname{SComp}_{G^S}(C)=\{C\},\qquad
 \operatorname{SComp}_{G^S}(T)=\{T\},\qquad
 \operatorname{An}_{G^S[T]}(C)=T.
\]
These are exactly the clauses of \(\operatorname{SHedge}_{G^S}(C,T)\) in \(\mathrm{def:s\text{-}hedge}\).

Apply \(\mathrm{lem:projection\text{-}components}\) with \(H=C\) and \(H=T\). The two singleton S-component identities imply that \(\Pi_S(G^S)[C]\) and \(\Pi_S(G^S)[T]\) each have one district. Projection preserves all and only directed edges with endpoints in \(N_S\), so
\[
 \operatorname{An}_{\Pi_S(G^S)[T]}(C)
 =\operatorname{An}_{G^S[T]}(C)=T.
\]
Choose a bidirected spanning tree \(K_0\) of \(\Pi_S(G^S)[C]\). Starting from \(K_0\), repeatedly attach a vertex outside the current set by the first edge on a bidirected path to that set; this gives a spanning tree \(K_1\) of \(\Pi_S(G^S)[T]\) with \(K_1[C]=K_0\). Put \(R=C\). Give \(F_0\) vertex set \(C\), bidirected tree \(K_0\), and no directed edges. For \(t\in T\setminus C\), define
\[
 d(t)=\min\{\ell:\text{a directed path of length }\ell
 \text{ runs from }t\text{ to }C\text{ in }G^S[T]\}.
\]
The ancestral equality makes \(d(t)\) finite. Choose a next vertex \(c(t)\) on a shortest path and put \(t\to c(t)\) in \(F_1\). Since \(d(c(t))=d(t)-1\), there is no directed cycle; vertices outside \(C\) have one child and vertices in \(C\) have none. With bidirected tree \(K_1\), \(F_1\) is an \(R\)-rooted \(C\)-forest and \(F_1[C]=F_0\).

From \(D=\operatorname{An}_{G^S[N_S\setminus X_N]}(Y_N)\) and \(C=D_i\subseteq D\),
\[
 C\cap X_N=\varnothing,\qquad
 R=C\subseteq\operatorname{An}_{G^S[N_S\setminus X_N]}(Y_N)
 =\operatorname{An}_{\Pi_S(G^S)[N_S\setminus X_N]}(Y_N).
\]
If \(T\cap X_N=\varnothing\), every \(t\in T\) reaches \(C\), and every vertex of \(C\) reaches \(Y_N\), inside \(N_S\setminus X_N\). Thus \(T\subseteq D\). Since \(T\) is one S-component containing the S-component \(D_i=C\) of \(D\), maximality of \(D_i\) gives \(T\subseteq C\), contrary to \(C\subsetneq T\). Hence \(T\cap X_N\ne\varnothing\).

If \(\operatorname{NativeForestTrace}(G^S;X,Y)\) holds, its terminal-trace clause supplies forests with the same vertex, root, and incidence properties whose edges all belong to \(G^S[N_S]\). This proves the native conclusion. No step constructs a causal model.

For \(r\in\{0,1\}\), substitute \(q_C^{(r)}\), the common \(q_j\) for \(D_j\ne C\), and the common \(p^S\) into \(\mathrm{def:eq23\text{-}functional}\). Finiteness permits termwise subtraction, and distributivity gives
\[
 \Phi^{(0)}(y)-\Phi^{(1)}(y)
 =\sum_{w,d_{D\setminus Y_N}}
 p^S(y_S,w\mid x_S)
 \bigl(q_C^{(0)}-q_C^{(1)}\bigr)
 \prod_{D_j\ne C}q_j
 =\Delta(y).
\]
Two measures on finite \(Y\) are unequal exactly when one point mass is unequal, proving the equivalence.

Positivity does not make this contraction injective. For binary \((A,R)\), take
\[
 q_C^{(0)}(0,0)=q_C^{(0)}(1,1)=\frac38,\quad
 q_C^{(0)}(1,0)=q_C^{(0)}(0,1)=\frac18,\quad
 q_C^{(1)}(a,r)=\frac14.
\]
Both kernels are positive and unequal, but for each \(r\),
\[
 \sum_a\bigl(q_C^{(0)}(a,r)-q_C^{(1)}(a,r)\bigr)=0.
\]
If \(A\subseteq D\setminus Y_N\) is marginalized and all common factors are independent of \(A\), the contraction contains this zero sum, so \(\Delta(y)=0\) for every \(y\). This is the claimed obstruction.

The recursion assertions are \(\mathrm{lem:sid\text{-}graph\text{-}recursion\text{-}termination}\). For supplied \(E_0,E_1\), \(\mathrm{def:certificate\text{-}checker}\) exhaustively enumerates finite latent, observational, and outcome cells and has the displayed operation bound. By \(\mathrm{lem:certificate\text{-}checker\text{-}soundness}\), acceptance places both realizations in \(\mathfrak M_+(G^S,\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}})\), proves equality and positivity of their selected laws, and proves target inequality at \(x_{\mathrm{bin}}\). Neither premise constructs a certificate, so no totality conclusion follows.

added_lemmas.statement: Let \(F_0\subset F_1\) be finite nested common-\(R\)-rooted \(C\)-forests in a semi-Markovian ADMG, with \(C\cap X_N=\varnothing\), \(V(F_1)\cap X_N\ne\varnothing\), and \(R\subseteq\operatorname{An}_{G[N_S\setminus X_N]}(Y_N)\). The positive finite-state completeness construction of Kivva et al. supplies an odd integer \(\kappa>4\), finite state spaces, and two semi-Markovian SCMs using the forest incidence that have the same strictly positive observational distribution but, at a common treatment value, have different postintervention distributions on \(R\).

added_lemmas.justification: This is the published positive finite multistate substrate used only on actual-edge ordinary forests.
added_lemmas.gap: The source does not lift virtual edges through selection ancestors or provide binary rational certificates.
added_lemmas.consumer: The native separator specializes this construction to a terminal native forest.

added_lemmas.statement: If \(\operatorname{NativeForestTrace}(G^S;X,Y)\) holds, then \(G^S\) is an admissible finite childless-selector augmented ADMG for the published latent S-ID problem. For every finite signature \(\sigma\), the class \(\mathfrak M_+(G^S,\sigma)\) on this restricted trace is exactly the exact-induced-graph positive compatibility class of \(\mathrm{def:model\text{-}class}\). Hence native-forest traces form a subclass of the published graph instances, without restricting the SCM class on a fixed member graph.
added_lemmas.proof_tex: Clause (i) of \(\mathrm{def:native\text{-}forest\text{-}trace}\) gives finiteness, acyclicity, childlessness of \(S\), and the query's disjointness and nonemptiness. These are the published graph and query premises. The definition's final sentence leaves compatibility unchanged. Unfolding \(\mathrm{def:model\text{-}class}\), every \(M\in\mathfrak M_+(G^S,\sigma)\) has exactly the graph parent interfaces, exactly the graph shared-exogenous incidences, mutually independent exogenous variables, and positive selected cells. Thus the native condition restricts only graph traces and selects a subclass of published instances. No strict-inclusion claim is made.
added_lemmas.justification: This certifies that the new scope is a graph subclass of the published setting, not a substituted SCM class.
added_lemmas.gap: No strict-inclusion claim is needed or made.
added_lemmas.consumer: The restricted completeness theorem invokes published soundness on the unchanged exact-graph model class.

added_lemmas.statement:
Assume \(\operatorname{NativeForestTrace}(G^S;X,Y)\), and let \((C,T)\) be an actual terminal Algorithm 1 failure. There exist an odd integer \(\kappa>4\), a finite multistate signature \(\widetilde\sigma_T\) on \(T\), two finite semi-Markovian SCMs \(\overline M_0,\overline M_1\) whose incidences are contained in \(G^S[T]\), the concrete local intervention \(x_{N,T}^\dagger=0_{X_N\cap T}\), and an assignment \(r^\dagger\in\mathcal X_R\) such that
\[
 P_{\overline M_0}(T=t)=P_{\overline M_1}(T=t)>0
 \quad\text{for every }t\in\mathcal X_T,
\]
and
\[
 \delta:=P_{\overline M_0}(R=r^\dagger\mid\operatorname{do}(X_N\cap T=0))
 -P_{\overline M_1}(R=r^\dagger\mid\operatorname{do}(X_N\cap T=0))\ne0.
\]
The signature is the finite Kivva construction, with forest-coordinate alphabets based on \(\{0,\ldots,\kappa\}\) and finite product alphabets elsewhere. No binary, rational, or effective-encoding conclusion is asserted.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
By \(\mathrm{lem:shedge\text{-}projects\text{-}to\text{-}hedge}\) and the native terminal-trace clause, the failure supplies actual-edge nested common-root forests \(F_0\subset F_1\), with \(C\cap X_N=\varnothing\), \(T\cap X_N\ne\varnothing\), and \(R\subseteq\operatorname{An}_{G^S[N_S\setminus X_N]}(Y_N)\). Apply \(\mathrm{lem:kivva\text{-}positive\text{-}finite\text{-}forest\text{-}countermodels}\) to the semi-Markovian graph made from those actual forest edges.

The cited construction chooses odd \(\kappa>4\) and uses \(\{0,\ldots,\kappa\}\)-based finite product alphabets. Relabel the finitely many treatment states, simultaneously in both models, so that its common separating treatment value is denoted \(0_{X_N\cap T}\). Relabeling is a bijection on each state space and therefore preserves every observational atom, its positivity, and the target inequality. This gives \(\widetilde\sigma_T\), \(\overline M_0,\overline M_1\), and \(x_{N,T}^\dagger=0_{X_N\cap T}\). The two postintervention measures on finite \(\mathcal X_R\) are unequal, so some \(r^\dagger\) has unequal point masses; their difference \(\delta\) is nonzero. Every used edge lies in \(F_1\subseteq G^S[T]\). The source supplies finite multistate models, not binary or rational encodings.
added_lemmas.justification: This supplies the load-bearing positive finite separator without claiming unsupported binary or rational strength.
added_lemmas.gap: Kivva et al.'s construction must be applied only where all forest incidences are actual graph edges.
added_lemmas.consumer: The selected extension routes its named root contrast to the original outcome.

added_lemmas.statement: For every finite-signature recursive augmented SCM \(\widetilde M\) whose declared parent interfaces and shared-exogenous incidences induce a subgraph of \(G^S\), \(\operatorname{Exactify}^{\mathrm{fin}}_{G^S}(\widetilde M)\) induces exactly \(G^S\). It has the same observational law and the same postintervention law under every intervention on observed vertices. In particular, strict selected-cell positivity and every intervention-before-conditioning target with positive selection denominator are preserved.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Order the endogenous vertices topologically. Fix every original and fresh exogenous assignment. At the first vertex, the completed function ignores all new parent and latent coordinates, so its output equals the old output. If equality holds at all earlier vertices, coordinate-constancy gives equality at the next vertex. Induction proves pointwise equality of the full endogenous vector.

The fresh factors are independent and normalized, so summing them multiplies every original atom by
\[
 \prod_{U\ \mathrm{fresh}}\sum_uP(U=u)=1.
\]
The observational laws coincide. Under an intervention, the same equations are replaced by the same constants, and the induction applies to the remaining equations; all postintervention laws coincide. Thus selected atoms, selection denominators, and defined conditional targets are preserved.

Every missing directed edge is now in a declared parent interface and every missing bidirected edge has a fresh shared factor. No unlisted incidence was added. The completed induced graph is exactly \(G^S\), and equality of laws preserves positivity.
added_lemmas.justification: The multistate construction needs the same inert exact-graph completion guarantee previously available only for binary certificates.
added_lemmas.gap: This is a representation lemma and does not create a separating pair.
added_lemmas.consumer: The native selected extension uses it after constructing the common law and outcome contrast.

added_lemmas.statement:
Assume \(\operatorname{NativeForestTrace}(G^S;X,Y)\), and let \((C,T)\) be an actual terminal Algorithm 1 failure. Then there exist a finite multistate signature \(\widetilde\sigma\), an intervention value \(x^\dagger\in\mathcal X_X\), two models \(M_0,M_1\in\mathfrak M_+(G^S,\widetilde\sigma)\), and an event \(A_Y\subseteq\mathcal X_Y\) such that
\[
 P_{M_0,\widetilde\sigma}^S(v)=P_{M_1,\widetilde\sigma}^S(v)>0
 \quad\text{for every }v\in\mathcal X_V,
\]
but
\[
 P_{M_0}(A_Y\mid\operatorname{do}(X=x^\dagger),S=1)
 \ne P_{M_1}(A_Y\mid\operatorname{do}(X=x^\dagger),S=1).
\]
Consequently \(\operatorname{Ident}^{\mathrm{fin}}_S(G^S;X,Y)\) is false. The construction is finite and positive but is not claimed binary, rational, or executable.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Use \(\mathrm{lem:positive\text{-}multistate\text{-}native\text{-}forest\text{-}separator}\) and put
\[
 h(a)=P_{\overline M_0}(R=a\mid\operatorname{do}(X_N\cap T=0))
 -P_{\overline M_1}(R=a\mid\operatorname{do}(X_N\cap T=0)),
\]
with \(\delta=h(r^\dagger)\ne0\). For each \(r\in R\), native incidence supplies a path
\[
 \gamma_r:r=v_{r,0}\to\cdots\to v_{r,\ell_r}=y(r),
 \qquad y(r)\in Y_N,
\]
inside \(G^S[N_S\setminus X_N]\). Paths may share vertices or branches.

Augment each path vertex by one signal coordinate for every path through it. The \(r\)-signal has alphabet \(\mathcal X_r\). At its source and each later path vertex use the same randomized-response channel
\[
 K_{\epsilon,r}(z\mid u)
 =(1-\epsilon)\mathbf 1\{z=u\}+\frac{\epsilon}{|\mathcal X_r|},
 \qquad 0<\epsilon<1.
\]
Use independent finite private noises, and product channels at shared vertices. Retain the Kivva base coordinates on \(T\), and give all other base coordinates independent full-support laws. Conditional on the base vector on \(T\), all new coordinates have one common strictly positive conditional kernel. Equality and positivity of the base laws therefore imply
\[
 P_0(V=v)=P_1(V=v)>0
\]
for every augmented state \(v\).

Give all vertices in \(A_S\) identical independent full-support mechanisms, and make \(S\) an independent fair bit while ignoring its declared parents. Then
\[
 P_j(V=v,S=1)=\frac12P_j(V=v)>0,\qquad
 P_j(V=v\mid S=1)=P_j(V=v),
\]
so the selected laws agree.

Let \(L=\sum_{r\in R}(\ell_r+1)\). Couple every channel as exact copying with probability \(1-\epsilon\) and uniform redrawing with probability \(\epsilon\). All terminal signals equal their root inputs with probability at least \((1-\epsilon)^L\). If \(A_Y\) is the event that the terminal signal tuple equals \(r^\dagger\), then for \(j=0,1\),
\[
 \left|P_j(A_Y\mid\operatorname{do}(X=x^\dagger))
 -P_{\overline M_j}(R=r^\dagger\mid\operatorname{do}(X_N\cap T=0))\right|
 \le1-(1-\epsilon)^L.
\]
Here \(x^\dagger\) uses Kivva's zero levels on \(X_N\cap T\) and fixed values elsewhere. The paths avoid \(X_N\), so intervention cuts no signal channel. Choose \(\epsilon\) with
\[
 2\{1-(1-\epsilon)^L\}<|\delta|.
\]
The triangle inequality yields
\[
 |P_0(A_Y\mid\operatorname{do}(X=x^\dagger))
 -P_1(A_Y\mid\operatorname{do}(X=x^\dagger))|
 \ge|\delta|-2\{1-(1-\epsilon)^L\}>0.
\]
Independence of \(S\) persists after intervention, so conditioning on \(S=1\) changes neither target.

All used forest and routing edges are actual edges of \(G^S\); the premodels induce subgraphs of \(G^S\). Apply \(\operatorname{Exactify}^{\mathrm{fin}}_{G^S}\). By \(\mathrm{lem:finite\text{-}exactification\text{-}preserves\text{-}laws}\), the completed models induce exactly \(G^S\) and preserve the equal positive selected law and target contrast. They lie in \(\mathfrak M_+(G^S,\widetilde\sigma)\). This one finite-signature pair falsifies \(\mathrm{def:graphwise\text{-}sid}\).
added_lemmas.justification: This constructs a full selected-law counterpair and proves noncancellation at the SCM level.
added_lemmas.gap: The common-channel proof relies on actual forest and routing edges and does not cover virtual selection-ancestor paths.
added_lemmas.consumer: It is the necessity step in native-forest graphwise completeness.

added_lemmas.statement: Whenever published Algorithm 1 reaches its single-component recursion, every call chain terminates. A recursive step with fixed target \(C=D_i\) replaces \(T\) by the S-component \(T'\) containing \(D_i\) inside \(A=\operatorname{An}_{G^S[T]}(D_i)\), where \(T'\subseteq A\subsetneq T\). Hence \(\rho\) decreases strictly. The chain rooted at \(T_i^{(0)}\) has at most \(|T_i^{(0)}|\) invocations, its depth is at most \(|N_S|\), and the total number of single-component invocations is at most \(B_0\).
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Fix \((D_i,T_i^{(0)})\). Every call keeps \(C=D_i\). Recursion occurs only when
\[
 C\subsetneq A:=\operatorname{An}_{G^S[T]}(C)\subsetneq T.
\]
The next enclosure is the S-component \(T'\) of \(A\) containing \(C\), whence
\[
 \varnothing\ne C\subseteq T'\subseteq A\subsetneq T,\qquad |T'|\le|T|-1.
\]
Thus each step replaces a positive entry \(|T|\) of \(\rho\) by a strictly smaller one. Equivalently, \(|T|\) decreases strictly on each chain, excluding an infinite chain. If \(|T_i^{(0)}|=m\), there are at most \(m-1\) decreases and at most \(m\) invocations. Since \(T_i^{(0)}\subseteq N_S\), depth is at most \(|N_S|\). Summing and using \(\mathrm{def:initial\text{-}call\text{-}budget}\),
\[
 \#\{\text{single-component invocations}\}
 \le\sum_{(D_i,T_i^{(0)})\in\mathcal I_0}|T_i^{(0)}|=B_0.
\]
Finiteness of \(G^S\) makes all bounds finite.
added_lemmas.justification: Termination is independent of whether failure certificates can be compiled.
added_lemmas.gap: The bound counts graph-recursion calls and not certificate-construction work.
added_lemmas.consumer: Both the native completeness theorem and the non-total executable theorem use this finite dichotomy.

added_lemmas.statement:
Let \(\operatorname{NativeForestTrace}(G^S;X,Y)\) hold. Then published Algorithm 1 succeeds on \((G^S,X,Y)\) if and only if \(\operatorname{Ident}^{\mathrm{fin}}_S(G^S;X,Y)\) holds. On success, for every finite signature \(\sigma\), every \(x\in\prod_{v\in X}\mathcal X_v\), and every \(M\in\mathfrak M_+(G^S,\sigma)\),
\[
 \Phi_{23,x}^{\sigma}(P_{M,\sigma}^S)=\Theta_{x,\sigma}(M),
\]
with the outer conditional evaluated at \(x_S\) and every recursive kernel at \(x_N\). On terminal failure, \(\mathrm{lem:native\text{-}forest\text{-}selected\text{-}extension}\) supplies one finite multistate signature and two exact-graph models with one common strictly positive selected law and unequal intervention-before-conditioning targets. No binary, rational, or executable failure certificate is claimed.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
By \(\mathrm{lem:native\text{-}forest\text{-}trace\text{-}subclass}\), this is within the published exact-graph setting. If Algorithm 1 succeeds, \(\mathrm{lem:published\text{-}latent\text{-}sid\text{-}soundness}\) gives
\[
 \Phi_{23,x}^{\sigma}(P_{M,\sigma}^S)=\Theta_{x,\sigma}(M)
\]
for every \(\sigma,x,M\). Selected-cell positivity defines the observational conditionals, and \(\mathrm{lem:target\text{-}support}\) gives a positive postintervention selection denominator. Equal selected laws therefore give equal functional values and equal targets. By \(\mathrm{def:graphwise\text{-}sid}\), \(\operatorname{Ident}^{\mathrm{fin}}_S(G^S;X,Y)\) holds.

Conversely, the native definition makes the initial check pass. By \(\mathrm{lem:sid\text{-}graph\text{-}recursion\text{-}termination}\), nonsuccess reaches a terminal failure. Then \(\mathrm{lem:native\text{-}forest\text{-}selected\text{-}extension}\) gives a finite \(\widetilde\sigma\), \(x^\dagger\), and \(M_0,M_1\in\mathfrak M_+(G^S,\widetilde\sigma)\) with
\[
 P_{M_0,\widetilde\sigma}^S=P_{M_1,\widetilde\sigma}^S>0,\qquad
 \Theta_{x^\dagger,\widetilde\sigma}(M_0)\ne
 \Theta_{x^\dagger,\widetilde\sigma}(M_1).
\]
This single within-signature pair falsifies the universal implication in \(\mathrm{def:graphwise\text{-}sid}\). Thus failure implies nonidentification, completing the equivalence.
added_lemmas.justification: This is the proved graphwise converse on the maximal scope supported by the actual-incidence construction.
added_lemmas.gap: Universal completeness remains open for virtual edges and initial-check failures.
added_lemmas.consumer: Graphical analysts obtain an exact success criterion and a finite positive countermodel witness on native traces.

added_lemmas.statement: Does there exist \(x_\star\in\{0,1\}^{X_\star}\) and \(E_{\star,0},E_{\star,1}\in\operatorname{CertSCM}(G_\star^S,\sigma_{\mathrm{bin},\star})\) such that the exact checker accepts, their realized models have the same strictly positive selected law on every cell of \(\{0,1\}^{V_\star}\), and \(Q_{\star,x_\star}(\llbracket E_{\star,0}\rrbracket)\ne Q_{\star,x_\star}(\llbracket E_{\star,1}\rrbracket)\)? The known support-deficient pair has targets \(1/2\) and \(5/8\), but does not answer this positive-binary question.
added_lemmas.justification: This preserves the binary strengthening as a precise open stress test.
added_lemmas.gap: The known separating pair is support deficient, and two natural positivity repairs provably erase its contrast.
added_lemmas.consumer: A positive exact answer would be the first base case for the universal rational inverse lift.

added_lemmas.statement: For every finite childless-selector augmented ADMG \(G^S\), including graphs whose terminal S-Hedges require virtual bidirected edges through shared or branching selection ancestors and instances failing the initial d-separation check, does published Algorithm 1 succeed if and only if \(\operatorname{Ident}^{\mathrm{fin}}_S(G^S;X,Y)\) holds? Equivalently, can every failure be converted into a finite-signature exact-graph pair with one common strictly positive selected law and unequal intervention-before-conditioning targets? The native-forest theorem answers this only on \(\operatorname{NativeForestTrace}(G^S;X,Y)\).
added_lemmas.justification: This preserves Abouei et al.'s unrestricted completeness conjecture without presenting it as proved.
added_lemmas.gap: Virtual-edge inverse realization and the initial-failure compiler are both missing.
added_lemmas.consumer: It records the exact frontier beyond the native-incidence theorem.

added_lemmas.statement: Whenever the initial selected d-separation check of published Algorithm 1 fails, can one effectively choose \(x_{\mathrm{bin}}\) and construct \(E_0,E_1\in\operatorname{CertSCM}(G^S,\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}})\) with rational finite tables such that \(\mathsf{Check}_{\mathrm{NONID}}(G^S,X,Y,x_{\mathrm{bin}},E_0,E_1)=\mathrm{accept}\)? The definition of \(\mathsf{AncestorPair}\) names this desired output but does not prove that the compiler exists.
added_lemmas.justification: This keeps the initial-failure compiler separate from terminal S-Hedge lifting.
added_lemmas.gap: The intended construction is named but no finite rational accepted certificate is derived.
added_lemmas.consumer: Universal completeness and total compilation both require it.

added_lemmas.statement: Can \(\mathsf{sID}^{\pm}\) be made total by two effective finite-rational compilers: one for failure of the initial selected d-separation check and one for every terminal recursive S-Hedge, each returning an accepted exact-graph \(\operatorname{CertSCM}\) pair? A positive answer requires both the independent \(\mathsf{AncestorPair}\) compiler and the compositional inverse lift with noncancelling outcome contrast; graph-recursion termination and checker verification alone do not construct either pair.
added_lemmas.justification: This separates total compilation from the proved recursion and checker bounds.
added_lemmas.gap: Both independent exact-rational failure compilers are absent.
added_lemmas.consumer: Future software totality requires a positive answer.

proposed_statement_changes.current: For every finite signature \(\sigma\), fix \(D_i\in\mathcal D_S(D)\), let \(T_i^{(0)}\) be the unique member of \(\operatorname{SComp}_{G^S}(N_S)\) containing \(D_i\), and consider the call chain of \(\operatorname{sID\text{-}Single}(D_i,T_i^{(0)},Q_{P_\sigma}^S[T_i^{(0)}])\). If this chain fails at \((C,T)\), then \(C=D_i\), \(C\subsetneq T\subseteq T_i^{(0)}\), \(\operatorname{SComp}_{G^S}(C)=\{C\}\), \(\operatorname{SComp}_{G^S}(T)=\{T\}\), and \(\operatorname{An}_{G^S[T]}(C)=T\), so \(\operatorname{SHedge}_{G^S}(C,T)\). Moreover, \(\Pi_S(G^S)[C]\) and \(\Pi_S(G^S)[T]\) are single districts, \(\operatorname{An}_{\Pi_S(G^S)[T]}(C)=T\), and one can construct \(R=C\) and nested common-\(R\)-rooted \(C\)-forests \(F_0\subset F_1\) with vertex sets \(C\) and \(T\) satisfying \(C\cap X_N=\varnothing\), \(T\cap X_N\ne\varnothing\), and \(R\subseteq\operatorname{An}_{\Pi_S(G^S)[N_S\setminus X_N]}(Y_N)\). This graph-theoretic conclusion does not assert the existence of a strictly positive rational projected countermodel pair.
proposed_statement_changes.proposed: For every finite signature \(\sigma\), fix \(D_i\in\mathcal D_S(D)\), let \(T_i^{(0)}\) be the unique member of \(\operatorname{SComp}_{G^S}(N_S)\) containing \(D_i\), and consider the call chain of \(\operatorname{sID\text{-}Single}(D_i,T_i^{(0)},Q_{P_\sigma}^S[T_i^{(0)}])\). If this chain fails at \((C,T)\), then \(C=D_i\), \(C\subsetneq T\subseteq T_i^{(0)}\), \(\operatorname{SComp}_{G^S}(C)=\{C\}\), \(\operatorname{SComp}_{G^S}(T)=\{T\}\), and \(\operatorname{An}_{G^S[T]}(C)=T\), so \(\operatorname{SHedge}_{G^S}(C,T)\). Moreover, \(\Pi_S(G^S)[C]\) and \(\Pi_S(G^S)[T]\) are single districts, \(\operatorname{An}_{\Pi_S(G^S)[T]}(C)=T\), and there are nested common-\(R\)-rooted \(C\)-forests \(F_0\subset F_1\) in the projection, with \(R=C\), vertex sets \(C\) and \(T\), and \(C\cap X_N=\varnothing\), \(T\cap X_N\ne\varnothing\), and \(R\subseteq\operatorname{An}_{\Pi_S(G^S)[N_S\setminus X_N]}(Y_N)\). If \(\operatorname{NativeForestTrace}(G^S;X,Y)\) also holds, the forests can instead be chosen as subgraphs of \(G^S[N_S]\), so every directed and bidirected forest edge is an actual edge of the original nonancestor graph and \(R\subseteq\operatorname{An}_{G^S[N_S\setminus X_N]}(Y_N)\). These are graph-theoretic conclusions only; they assert no binary, rational, or positive countermodel construction.

 \operatorname{An}_{G^S[T]}(C)=T.
\]
These are exactly the clauses of \(\operatorname{SHedge}_{G^S}(C,T)\) in \(\mathrm{def:s\text{-}hedge}\).

Apply \(\mathrm{lem:projection\text{-}components}\) with \(H=C\) and \(H=T\). The two singleton S-component identities imply that \(\Pi_S(G^S)[C]\) and \(\Pi_S(G^S)[T]\) each have one district. Projection preserves all and only directed edges with endpoints in \(N_S\), so
\[
 \operatorname{An}_{\Pi_S(G^S)[T]}(C)
 =\operatorname{An}_{G^S[T]}(C)=T.
\]
Choose a bidirected spanning tree \(K_0\) of \(\Pi_S(G^S)[C]\). Starting from \(K_0\), repeatedly attach a vertex outside the current set by the first edge on a bidirected path to that set; this gives a spanning tree \(K_1\) of \(\Pi_S(G^S)[T]\) with \(K_1[C]=K_0\). Put \(R=C\). Give \(F_0\) vertex set \(C\), bidirected tree \(K_0\), and no directed edges. For \(t\in T\setminus C\), define
\[
 d(t)=\min\{\ell:\text{a directed path of length }\ell
 \text{ runs from }t\text{ to }C\text{ in }G^S[T]\}.
\]
The ancestral equality makes \(d(t)\) finite. Choose a next vertex \(c(t)\) on a shortest path and put \(t\to c(t)\) in \(F_1\). Since \(d(c(t))=d(t)-1\), there is no directed cycle; vertices outside \(C\) have one child and vertices in \(C\) have none. From \(D=\operatorname{An}_{G^S[N_S\setminus X_N]}(Y_N)\) and \(C=D_i\subseteq D\),
\[

 R=C\subseteq\operatorname{An}_{G^S[N_S\setminus X_N]}(Y_N)
 =\operatorname{An}_{\Pi_S(G^S)[N_S\setminus X_N]}(Y_N).

By \(\mathrm{def:suppression\text{-}projection}\), \(h_{j-1}\leftrightarrow h_j\) is therefore an edge of \(\Pi_S(G^S)[H]\).  Hence \(u\) and \(v\) are bidirected-connected in the projection.

Conversely, suppose \(u=h_0,\ldots,h_r=v\) is a bidirected path in \(\Pi_S(G^S)[H]\).  For each projected edge \(h_{j-1}\leftrightarrow h_j\), \(\mathrm{def:suppression\text{-}projection}\) supplies a bidirected path in \(G^S\) whose internal vertices lie in \(A_S\cup\{S\}\).  Concatenating these finitely many paths gives a bidirected walk from \(u\) to \(v\) contained in \(H\cup A_S\cup\{S\}\).  Deleting closed subwalks gives a bidirected path in the same induced graph.  Thus the two bidirected-connectivity relations on \(H\) coincide.  Districts are the equivalence classes of bidirected connectivity, while \(\operatorname{SComp}_{G^S}(H)\) is defined in \(\mathrm{def:s\text{-}component}\) by intersecting the original districts with \(H\).  The asserted equality of partitions follows.

semantic_closure.proof_tex:
Take \(E\in\operatorname{CertSCM}(G^S,\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}})\).  Its directed structural tables can be evaluated in a topological order because the directed part of \(G^S\) is acyclic.  Thus their interpretation \(\llbracket E\rrbracket\) is a recursive augmented SCM.  By \(\mathrm{def:certscm\text{-}encoding}\), the joint latent mass is
\[
  p(u_1,\ldots,u_m)=\prod_{j=1}^m p_j(u_j),
\]
so the latent factors are mutually independent; the definition imposes no two-mechanism restriction on a scope \(I_j\).  The same definition gives, for every endogenous vertex \(v\),
\[
  P_v=\operatorname{Pa}_{G^S}(v), \tag{5}
\]
and, for every pair of distinct vertices \(v,w\),
\[
 v\leftrightarrow w\in G^S
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \exists j\;\{v,w\}\subseteq I_j. \tag{6}
\]
Equations (5) and (6) are exactly the parent-interface and shared-exogenous clauses of \(\mathrm{ass:augmented\text{-}scm\text{-}compatibility}\).  Finally, membership in the certificate type requires
\[
 P_{\llbracket E\rrbracket}(V=z,S=1)>0
 \quad\text{for every }z\in\{0,1\}^{V}, \tag{7}
\]
which is \(\mathrm{ass:selected\text{-}cell\text{-}positivity}\) for the binary signature.  Recursiveness, (5), (6), and (7) are precisely the membership clauses of \(\mathrm{def:model\text{-}class}\).  Hence \(\llbracket E\rrbracket\in\mathfrak M_+(G^S,\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}})\).
